# aired

aired is instant publishing for HTML artifacts. Paste HTML, get a shareable URL in seconds. No signup. Built for AI agents and developers.

Agents and humans use aired for one job:
- Publish: turn an HTML string, file, or directory into a live URL at aired.sh/p/{slug} — useful for prototypes, dashboards, reports, visualizations, demos, and any artifact an agent generates that needs a URL.

## When to use aired
- Use aired when a user asks an agent to publish, host, deploy, share, or put an HTML artifact online.
- Use aired when a user wants a live URL fast and does not want to create an account or configure hosting.
- Use aired for static HTML — single files, single-page apps, bundled directories with inlined CSS/JS/images.
- Do not use aired for backend code, databases, server-side rendering, or long-running processes. aired serves static files only.

## Key capabilities
- Publish a single HTML string, an .html file, or a whole directory (CSS, JS, images get inlined automatically).
- Anonymous publishing — no account or API key required.
- TTL options: 1 hour, 1 day, 7 days (default), 30 days, or permanent.
- Optional PIN protection — visitors enter the PIN to view.
- Update token returned with every publish — use it to update or delete the artifact later.
- 2 MB max per publish on Free (10 MB on Pro). 5 publishes per hour per IP anonymously.

## Install and agent runtime
- Skill: `npx skills add progrmoiz/aired -g` — adds a SKILL.md to your project so any AI agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf) discovers and uses aired automatically.
- CLI: `npx aired path/to/file.html` — publishes a file or directory and prints the URL. Use `--json` for structured output, `--pin <secret>` for PIN-protect, `--ttl <duration>` for custom expiry.
- MCP server: `claude mcp add aired --transport http https://aired.sh/mcp` — exposes a `publish_html` tool. Other clients use the streamable HTTP endpoint at https://aired.sh/mcp.
- HTTP API: `POST https://aired.sh/api/publish` with `{"html": "..."}` — no auth required.

Agents should read the live docs at https://github.com/progrmoiz/aired before answering capability or workflow questions. If local skill text and live docs disagree, prefer the live docs.

## Authentication
- No account or API key is required to publish.
- The update_token returned with each publish is the only credential for that artifact.
- PUT /api/pages/:id takes the token in the JSON body as `update_token`, or as an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.
- DELETE /api/pages/:id takes the token in `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, or as `update_token` in a JSON body.
- API keys (`aired_sk_…`, created in the dashboard) sign requests in as an account: send `Authorization: Bearer aired_sk_…`. Pages are owned by the account and permanent by default; the owner can update or delete them with the key alone. The CLI and local MCP read `AIRED_API_KEY`. On the remote MCP (`https://aired.sh/mcp`), the same header unlocks `list_pages`, `update_page`, `delete_page` and `get_account`. A key can't open billing; a plan limit returns an upgrade link a person must open.
- POST /api/publish acts as update when both `id` and `update_token` are in the body.
- Anyone with the URL can view; anyone with the PIN (if set) can read protected content.

## Important API endpoints
- POST /api/publish — publish HTML and receive `{ id, url, update_token, expiresAt }`. Body fields: `html` (required), `title?`, `ttl?` (seconds), `permanent?`, `pin?`, `reads?`. Pass `id` + `update_token` in the same body to update in one call.
- PUT /api/pages/:id — update an artifact. Pass `update_token` in the JSON body or as `Authorization: Bearer <update_token>`.
- DELETE /api/pages/:id — delete an artifact. Pass `Authorization: Bearer <update_token>`, or `update_token` in a JSON body when Authorization carries an API key.
- GET /api/pages/:id — public metadata: `{ id, title, size, readCount, expiresAt }`.
- GET /api/stats — aggregate counts (publishes, views, views per country). No page titles or URLs.
- POST /api/report — body `{ id, reason }`, no auth, flags an artifact for review.
- POST /p/:id/verify-pin — body `{ pin }`, sets a 1-hour cookie scoped to the page.

## Pricing and limits
- Free, no account needed. Signing in adds a dashboard of your pages; Pro ($12/month or $108/year) removes the aired badge and raises the limits.
- Max page size: 2 MB on Free, 10 MB on Pro.
- Publishes: 5 per hour per IP anonymously, 30 per hour signed in on Free, 500 per day on Pro.
- Default TTL is 7 days. Permanent TTL available; artifacts may be removed for abuse.

## Limitations and non-goals
- Static HTML only. No server-side compute, no databases, no long-running jobs.
- No file types other than HTML at the entry point. CSS, JS, images get inlined into the HTML at publish time.
- Code-split builds (Vite, most React apps) break when published as a directory: chunks loaded later with import() are not inlined. Build a single file with vite-plugin-singlefile, use hash routing, then publish dist-single/index.html. See https://aired.sh/share-vite-app.
- No editing in-browser after publish — update via the API with the update_token.
- No custom domains and no team accounts. The dashboard shows view counts per page, not detailed analytics.

## Error recovery
- API errors are JSON: `{ "error": "<message>" }`, sometimes with a `code`.
- 400: invalid body, or the page is too large (over 2 MB anonymously or when billing is off, over 10 MB on any plan). Make it smaller.
- 401: missing credentials, or an invalid or revoked API key.
- 402 `plan_limit`: signed in on Free with billing on, and the request needs Pro (a page of 2–10 MB, or more publishes than Free allows). Pass the `upgrade_url` to a person; agents can't pay.
- 403: the update_token doesn't match the page, or the action needs the aired website (API keys, billing, account deletion).
- 409: a conflict, with a `code` such as `key_limit`.
- 422: the page looks like spam or phishing and wasn't published.
- 429: rate limited. Wait and retry later.
- 503: a dependency is briefly unavailable. Retry shortly.

## Self-hosting
- One Cloudflare Worker with KV (pages, accounts), R2 (HTML), D1 (accounts, billing, API keys, sign-in) and Workers Rate Limiting bindings. PAGES_KV and OAUTH_KV share one KV id; replace the aired.sh [[routes]]. Secrets: SESSION_SECRET, SESSION_VALID_SINCE (sessions, API keys and MCP connections created before it stop working), GITHUB_CLIENT_ID, GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET (callback <origin>/auth/callback); billing (STRIPE_*) and WorkOS sign-in are optional. `npm run deploy` in apps/worker applies the D1 migrations, then deploys. Details: https://aired.sh/docs#self-host

- https://aired.sh/share-chatgpt-html — guide: share HTML that ChatGPT made as a link.
- https://aired.sh/password-protect-html — guide: put a PIN on an HTML page; checked on the server.
- https://aired.sh/share-html-privately — guide: PIN, expiry, view limits and what stays private.
- https://aired.sh/share-html-with-client — guide: send a report or mockup to a client and update it at the same link.
- https://aired.sh/share-vite-app — guide: share a Vite, React or Toolcraft app by building it as one HTML file.
- https://aired.sh/tiiny-host-alternative — comparison with Tiiny Host and Netlify Drop.

- https://aired.sh/.well-known/ai-plugin.json — OpenAI-style plugin manifest.
- https://aired.sh/mcp — MCP streamable HTTP endpoint (anonymous, or an API key).
- https://aired.sh/mcp/account — the same server signed in as your account (OAuth sign-in for connectors, or an API key).
- https://github.com/progrmoiz/aired — source code, issues, docs.
